newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Aspiration seen narrowly winning Thai poll.
newsitem.headline: New Aspiration seen narrowly winning Thai poll.

text.p: The New Aspiration Party (NAP) of Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh was seen as the winner of the Thai general election by a slim margin, according to television projections late on Sunday.

Most television stations put the NAP ahead of its rival the Democrat Party of former premier Chuan Leekpai by a close margin of about two seats. The main Channel 9 projection of unofficial results, eight hours after the poll closed at 0800 GMT, showed the NAP in front with 125 seats to the Democrats 123 in the the 393-seat parliament.

Earlier, Chavalit said that he sensed victory and appeared together with the leaders of four other parties at a news conference in a show of unity. Among the party leaders with him was outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa, head of the Chart Thai party expected to win about 40 seats.
Several political commentators said on television that it looked likely that the NAP could be the core party around which a new coalition government could emerge for Thailand.
The Democrat party's Chuan said he acknowledged unofficial reports that his party was traiing the NAP by slim margin. But official results are not due until Monday morning.
This election, said by analysts to be the most violent and dirty in two decades, was seen as a close one with the NAP and Democrats running neck and neck until campaigning was over.
